verdict.rationale: Smithery's own CLI provides runtime tool discovery and invocation: `smithery tool find` searches tools by name or intent and `smithery tool call` invokes one on a connection. An agent could therefore search for and call tools on demand rather than preloading every definition. However, nothing documents these as MCP meta-tools exposed inside an agent's context, or explicitly frames them as a context-saving alternative to loading full tool lists. The probe noting an official MCP server gives no detail on search or load meta-tools. Missing for 10: documented in-context meta-tools (search/load tools) exposed to agents via MCP or API, explicit context-reduction design, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can search and load tools at runtime through meta-tools instead of having thousands of tool definitions stuffed into my context

citations.quote: smithery tool find [query]             # Search tools by name or intent
smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]  # Call a tool
